cli.fuzzed: The CLI shell wires argv into the engine and renders results. Every parser it calls (parse_target, parse_port_spec, options) carries its own fuzz target; it has no parse entry point of its own.

congestion.fuzzed: AIMD congestion-window arithmetic over our own scheduler state. Replies are classified and validated by core before any number reaches here, so no attacker-controlled bytes are parsed.

core::log.fuzzed: Verbosity-level accessors (init, verbosity, debugging). Holds no attacker data and renders no strings.

core::nse::engine.fuzzed: Drives the VM through nse_main.lua's own scheduler and stores results; the bytes a script returns reach output only through core::nse::results, which nse_results fuzzes against transliterations of the C. Exercised end to end by scripts_differential (37 scenarios against nmap 7.94), including the cnse functions' argument checks.

core::nse::lfs.fuzzed: Binding only: lfs.mkdir hands the path bytes, as luaL_checkstring gives them, to the host's ScriptFs, and get_path_separator returns a constant. It parses nothing; the policy it asks (core::nse::fspolicy) is covered by nse_scriptargs and sys::nsefs's tests. Exercised end to end against nmap 7.94 by nse_cli_differential's lfs and http-fetch scenarios, results and trees byte for byte.

core::nse::net.fuzzed: The script-facing half of NSE sockets: it checks a script's arguments (ports, protocols, timeouts, families) as nse_nsock.cc checks them and hands data to the host as opaque bytes. It parses no network data; receive_buf's delimiter search is in the prelude's Lua, on the VM's own pattern matcher, which is fuzzed. Exercised end to end by nse_net_differential (three scenarios against nmap 7.94, every argument error included), and pinned by sabotage.

core::nse::openssl.fuzzed: Binding only: reads Lua arguments through the shared LuaArgs and type_error helpers and hands bytes and integers to core::nse::openssl::bn and ::digest, which nse_openssl_bignum and nse_openssl_digest fuzz, and lengths to the randomness seam. Exercised against nmap 7.94 by openssl_bn_differential's 11,171 rows and openssl_digest_differential's 2,322, among them every function with every wrong argument type.

core::nse::openssl::rand.fuzzed: No parser: fills a caller's buffer from the OS CSPRNG (getrandom), seedable only under cfg(test). Gated by its non-constancy tests.

core::nse::package.fuzzed: require's loader: library names come from scripts and libraries nmap ships, and files are read only through the LibrarySource it is given. The chunks it compiles go to the VM's own parser. Exercised end to end by nselib_differential, which requires all 133 shipped libraries against nmap 7.94.

core::nse::runtime.fuzzed: Builds the NSE state from fixed parts and runs the fixed prelude. Takes no input beyond the configuration the host passes. Exercised by nselib_differential and the prelude's verbatim test.

core::nse::stdlib.fuzzed: Binding only: converts Lua values with the VM's own conversions and hands every byte of script- or packet-supplied data to the pure modules core::nse::stdlib::strpack, ::pattern, ::strformat and ::strrep, which carry the nse_strpack, nse_pattern, nse_format and nse_tail targets. Nothing here parses input. It is exercised end to end by the strpack, pattern, format and tail differentials, and by in-module tests Miri runs, including the gsub and format sequences that call back into the VM.

core::nse::stdlib::debuglib.fuzzed: Read-only introspection of the running VM's frames (patch 0010). It takes no data beyond a level number or a function, and is exercised by the stdlib differential's debug section and by strict.lua in every library load.

core::nse::stdlib::iolib.fuzzed: io over files the policy allows: nmap's own data files and files the operator named, not remote data. read_number is bounded by L_MAXLENNUM and hands its numeral to the VM's own conversion. Exercised by the 2,012-case stdlib differential against liblua/ over fixture files, and by in-module arithmetic justified per function.

core::trace.fuzzed: A single enabled() predicate over a verbosity flag. Takes no input of any kind.

engine.fuzzed: Scan scheduling and task orchestration over owned state. Every byte is parsed by a core parser before a result reaches the engine.

model.fuzzed: The result data model (Host, Port, PortState). Constructed by us from already-parsed values; it has no parse entry point.

net.fuzzed: Thin tokio socket wrappers. Anything received is handed to a core parser, each of which is separately fuzzed.

output.fuzzed: Renders ScanResults to normal, grepable and XML text. It parses nothing. Every attacker-derived string reaches it already escaped: -sV fields through the CLI's printable_escape (as portlist.cc's cstringSanityCheck), NSE output through core::nse::results (fuzzed by nse_results). XML attributes go through xml_escape, pinned by xml_is_well_formed_shape_and_escapes and os_names_and_classes_are_xml_escaped. Miri clean on its 28 tests (M6.4d retrospective); no unsafe. Exercised end to end by the M1 and M7 differentials.

sys::datadir.fuzzed: nmap_fetchfile's search order over directories the run gives it: it joins a file name onto each and asks the OS whether it is readable. It parses nothing. Pinned by unit tests (order, directories, absolute names, the working directory never searched) and by nse_cli_differential, with sabotage of the search caught.

sys::fpengine.fuzzed: I/O driver for the IPv6 fingerprint battery. Every byte-level decision delegates to core::fp6_match::is_response (fuzz target fp6_match); its only local slicing is network_layer(), a total frame.get(14..).unwrap_or(&[]).

sys::ndp.fuzzed: Neighbour-discovery I/O driver. Frame parsing is core::ndp::resolve_from_frame, covered by fuzz target ndp_advert; this module only drives the capture and the timeout.

sys::nsefs.fuzzed: The ScriptFs over the real file system: it resolves a path as open(2) and mkdir(2) do (canonicalising, with the lookup's own errors, PATH_MAX, trailing '.' and separators), asks fspolicy, and opens the canonical path with O_NOFOLLOW, refusing to write through a name that is a link leading nowhere. It builds the policy: output directories designated as they are or, when only missing, as their nearest existing ancestor and plain names (any other lookup error, '..' or a link leading nowhere refuses); and nothing writable that overlaps what nmap loads: every data directory in the search, existing or not, what links at its top or beneath its nselib/ and scripts/ lead to (a bounded walk), the chosen scripts, and on Unix hard links to those files. It parses nothing; the argument values it is given are fspolicy's, fuzzed by nse_scriptargs. Pinned by tests that cover escaping a data directory by .. and by symlink, dangling links (w, a, w+, a+, r+), the path shapes against the kernel's errnos, named files, output directories (existing, not yet existing, each refusal by reason), the overlap rules (absent data directory, linked nselib, nested link, hard link, chosen script), devices as read files, mkdir, and missing files; and end to end by nse_cli_differential's lfs and http-fetch scenarios against nmap 7.94 and its port-only file tests.

sys::nsehost.fuzzed: The host side of NSE: nselib/ and script lookup over the data directories, the interface list from sys::netif, random bytes from the OS, and a ScriptNet wrapper that timestamps polls. It parses no network or file data. Pinned by unit tests and exercised end to end by nse_cli_differential against nmap 7.94.

sys::nsenet.fuzzed: ScriptNet over tokio: connect, read, write and timers, with every read capped at MAX_READ (4 MiB). It parses nothing; the only logic over received bytes is counting newlines to decide when a read is satisfied, which a unit test pins (Miri clean). Exercised against live fixture services by nse_net_differential.

sys::osscan.fuzzed: OS-detection round driver. Frame parsing is core::osprobe::demux::demux, covered by fuzz target osprobe_demux (added in M7.1); this module does the bookkeeping around it.

sys::scan.fuzzed: Connect-scan driver over tokio sockets. No wire bytes are parsed here; port state comes from the syscall result.

sys::sigstore.fuzzed: Installs already-verified bytes to disk. The manifest parsing, and the single-path-component invariant install() relies on, are fuzzed in core by sigstore_manifest.

timing.fuzzed: RTT and timeout arithmetic over our own measurements. No untrusted-input parse path.
